title: [ORION-QG QG-9 T1] Exact n=4 cap-3 witness hunt for R6I support-four tightness
body:
Parent tightness programme: #762
Earned support<=4 theorem: #790 / PR #791
Theorem miner: #767

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE EXACT TIGHTNESS HUNT — witness or bounded negative, no preferred outcome.**

QG-13 V4 has now machine-checked `C_DP = C_cap4` for all n in the frozen R6I grammar. Tightness of four remains open. Exploratory anchored-slice analysis at support four finds 432 necessary QG-1-irreducible slices per generator orientation; the cumulative E2/E3 edit basis covers 396 and leaves 36 canonical obstruction slices. A four-column extension of the same globally-worst edit abstraction does not close those 36. These exploratory facts motivate the candidate generator but are not themselves tightness evidence.

T1 asks:

> Does there exist an n=4 R6I instance with a feasible support-4 compilation whose cost is strictly below the exact optimum over all configurations with every independent generator support<=3?

A single strict witness proves the all-n support<=4 theorem is tight.

## Why n=4

Support four cannot be necessary below four qubits. n=4 is therefore the minimal exact witness size.

## Frozen candidate generation — no cap3 scores allowed

Recompute from production semantics the canonical support-4 anchored obstruction slices for orientation g=0 and g=1:
- selected generator active on all four columns;
- selected anticommutation parity=1;
- selected two-bit Tag label nonzero;
- selected/partner N classes and C classes zero-sum-free;
- no globally safe E2/E3 move deletes the selected generator.

Candidate generation never calls the cap3 referee.

For each obstruction in canonical order:
1. choose, within each local structural type, the lexicographically first realization minimizing local Tag support `wt(s0)+wt(s1)`;
2. assemble desired block A (or B for orientation1) frame generators and shared Tag;
3. choose the other block's rank-2 frame pair by exhaustive n=4 search minimizing `(Uanti, total frame support, lexicographic frame codes)` subject to the **same ordered two Tag labels** under the chosen shared Tag;
4. set each block's target triple equal to its desired rank-2 frame triple `(R0,R1,R0R1)` — identity-Restore inverse design, the strongest target template for that desired frame under the frozen objective;
5. retain only candidates whose desired two-block frame/Tag configuration passes the production witness semantics; record its exact feasible cost `U4`.

Freeze a scan cap of the first **36 candidates per orientation** (72 maximum) in canonical obstruction order. Stop at the first strict tightness witness; do not widen the candidate grammar after outcome.

## Exact cap-3 referee

For each candidate compute

`C_cap3 = min cost over the full frozen R6I grammar with support(RA0), support(RA1), support(RB0), support(RB1) <=3`.

Use an exact MILP over the same production local option algebra, looped over the frozen 54 `(relative B permutation, central A, central B)` configurations.

For each fixed configuration:
- one binary variable selects one local option per qubit after exact dominance compression by `(10-bit delta, four-generator activity mask)`;
- ten parity equations enforce one of the six exact production accepting states, with integer parity-carry variables;
- four support inequalities enforce total generator activity<=3;
- objective is the exact production local raw cost, subtracting the frozen global Uanti constant only after optimization;
- accepting-state choice is encoded by six binary selector variables in the same MILP.

Solver: frozen SciPy/HiGHS stack available in ORION CI, `mip_rel_gap=0` / optimal termination required. Record solver/version/model dimensions, primal integrality residuals and every constraint residual.

Early rejection is allowed: if any fixed configuration proves `C_cap3 <= U4`, that candidate cannot be a tight witness and the remaining configurations for that candidate need not be solved. A **positive** candidate requires every one of the 54 fixed configurations solved optimally and global `C_cap3 > U4`.

## Tightness proof

If a candidate has a verified feasible support-4 configuration of cost U4 and exact `C_cap3 > U4`, then

`C_DP <= U4 < C_cap3`.

Therefore no support<=3 configuration is globally optimal, while V4 already proves some support<=4 optimum exists for every instance. Hence support four is necessary on that instance and the all-n support bound 4 is tight.

The feasible support-4 configuration does **not** need to be proven globally optimal for the strict-gap argument.

## Independent verification

Generic ORION harness:
- reconstruct candidate frame/Tag feasibility and U4 independently;
- rebuild the compressed MILP from the mathematical R6I specification without importing production `_DELTA` for any claimed positive;
- rerun all 54 fixed configs for a positive candidate;
- verify solver optimal status, integrality and exact objective recomputation.

Native ORION-Q harness keeps states:
- `TIGHT_WITNESS`
- `NO_WITNESS_IN_FROZEN_PANEL`
- `SOLVER_CANNOT_CHECK`
- `CANDIDATE_BINDING_FAILURE`

separate. A finite no-witness scan cannot imply support<=3 theorem authority.

## Honest terminals

- `QG9T1_R6I_SUPPORT4_TIGHT_WITNESS_EXACT`
- `QG9T1_NO_SUPPORT4_TIGHT_WITNESS_IN_FROZEN_PANEL`
- `QG9T1_CAP3_SOLVER_CANNOT_CHECK`
- `QG9T1_CANDIDATE_BINDING_FAILURE`

## Claim boundary

A positive is an exact mathematical tightness witness for the frozen R6I objective/grammar, not a physical quantum advantage. MILP/HiGHS, inverse design and support-capped optimization are donor methods. Novelty authority remains false pending external review.
